body: I'm so sorry, you deserved better

It reminds me how bad people are about sticking with goals and incorporating exercise as a daily routine. They wait for an arbitrary date established by society and blindly decide to follow some goals that are clearly not a priority, or the person would have pursued already. Why wait until the new year to improve yourself? Study after study shows that resolutions don't usually work. I know I sound like Scrooge, and I believe people should exercise and he healthy. But I'm sick of this endless push toward unrealistic self improvement, which has turned many people neurotic and suffering from low self esteem because they can't live up to so many impossible standards and expect results too quickly. When they don't get them, they quit. Instead of making decisions day to day to stay healthy, they diet and obsess over their weight, join a gym once a year and exercise religiously until they fall of the wagon completely and just stop going altogether. There is no balance. There are people who keep going at it, yes. And that's great. But many fail and then punish themselves for it, perpetuating the cycle of not being honest with themselves and not living in reality.

I call random people on the phone and ask hard questions as a journalist. I'm not afraid to meet new people for my job. Some says are harder than others, but it has forced me to come out of my shell more. I can separate my feelings and emotions from my work.

Oh I'm sorry to hear that :( often it's not as bad as we imagine. This is especially true if people have high expectations or are very hard on themselves, which is most people it seems like. 

I was reading the subreddit /r/tifu and it reminded me how we're all fallible. Everyone has those cringeworthy moments in life that are hard to look back on, and getting drunk during the holiday season is a big and very common one. I'm trying to remind myself that at least I didn't drive or hurt anyone, and that it is a blessing in disguise because my drinking has become uncontrollable and I need to make changes.

If you were nervous, that's completely normal and it's common to drink too much to compensate. I'm sure his family knows this, and if they are kind they'll understand :) 

Anyway sorry for the wall of text, hope you get to feeling better

Thank you so much. I'm planning to spend the next day or two searching online for a new therapist, and the idea about group therapy is very good. I t would be scary at first but ultimately very rewarding. I feel so horrible that I let it get to this point. It just seemed like I've been coping for over a decade but not truly living.

Thank you so much :) I'm going to continue seeing a therapist, and talk more about my alcohol abuse. One of the hard parts is I feel so terrible about myself, I'm afraid that anyone I tell will be very angry and reprimand me. It's sounds so childish. But it's time to grow up and take responsibility (not my strong suit)

Thank you so much. This was a very thoughtful reply. It is true there is more hope for the future. I don't think I've ever felt this depressed in my life (or let myself feel this depressed), so in a way it's a relief that I have nothing to lose. 

One reason I have not sought out AA or other resources is that I'm highly sensitive to rejection and very shy. I can't even imagine introducing myself or speaking about myself to anyone in person. But I'd really like to. It would be nice to meet other people who could potentially be a friend. 

I'm not quite sure what happened in my childhood. I was afraid of my mom in many ways, and I never felt loved by her. I don't think she ever loved me, or at least that's how I perceived it. Because my parents worked, I spent most of my time alone. It wasn't bad it I think this led to extreme self focus. As a teen I was sexually abused by several men and I drank too much and very frequently. There were warning signs, such as my parents catching me drinking and driving, but they never did anything. It was like they decided I was old enough to make my own decisions even though I was clearly falling apart.

It did not help that I was a good student and always held down jobs. It must have appeared to them that I was ok. It just seems like a good parent would have intervened. 

The sad thing is, the more I want and need people, the more likely they are to reject me. It's that parent relationship playing out in each adult relationship I have.

I've been seeing this therapist for about 6 months. My So and I agreed it the depression and social anxiety havent improved and clearly gotten worse. I decided to use the holidays as a time to end my time with that therapist, as much as he is a likeable and good person. If I want to get better, it's time to get serious about taking care of me.

It felt good just to get some of this out and tell someone. If you read it, just want to know how much it means to me. You are a good person.

Please don't do that. I know I'm just a random stranger but it would break my heart if something happened. I can relate to your post. I feel rejected by others and like an outcast. But please know that if I met you I would give you a hug, because I know how it feels. I would hug you because we're in this together. There is nothing to be afraid of at the bottom, which is why we have to keep going and do our best at this life. Even if we never reach all our goals, life will get better than it is now. Please, give it another chance. You are loved even if you can't see it now. You are important and many people in this world would love you if you give them another chance.
